MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Geelong Hospital

The Associate Nurse Unit Manager acts as a responsible and effective team member, assists in the overall clinical management of the ward, is responsible for the provision of comprehensive patient care and supervision of care given by junior staff in accordance with the Nurses and Midwifery Board of Australia Scope of Practice and deputises for and assists the Nursing Unit Manager.

3 North comprises an Oncology- Haematology - Palliative and Medical ward which brings together clinicians from a wide range of disciplines associated with cancer treatment, respiratory, endocrinology, renal and general medicine. We pride ourselves on providing a high standard of professional and multidisciplinary care with compassion and expertise.

We currently have a part-time opportunity available at a preferred 0.8 FTE, with flexibility to discuss arrangements for the right candidate.

The Position

Monitors staff levels against budget-target levels related to number of bed days, occupancy and patient acuity. Adjusts staffing levels in consultation with the Unit Manager and-or Coordinator according to changes in levels.

Provide leadership and direction to team in the absence of the Nursing Unit Manager and act as a role model and resource person.

Responsible for assisting the Nurse Unit Manager in following issues pertaining to human resources within the department and will assume full responsibility in the absence of the Nurse Unit Manager.

Maintains and promotes harmonious interpersonal relationships and effective team work between staff, patient, relative, doctors and ancillary staff.

Participate as a valued team member promoting and contributing to a supportive team environment.

Participate in, contribute to and implement quality improvement and risk management into all aspects of service.

Participate in the documentation of Risk Assessments and Standard Operating Procedures for activities that could pose an OHS risk.

Raise OHS issues with appropriate caregivers and take part in OHS consultative arrangements.

Assess education needs at a ward level and assist caregivers to maintain a high level of clinical nursing skills by providing on shift support and structured education sessions.

Demonstrates progress towards the achievement of goals and personal and professional growth.

You will have a registration with Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse and at least 2 years post graduate experience in Oncology nursing, have well developed analytical and problem-solving skills and knowledge of acts and legislation that impact on the practice of nursing. With demonstrated ability to develop and build effective nursing, medical and interdisciplinary relationships and teams. Previous experience in a clinical managerial role or experience being in charge of an acute ward will be highly regarded.

To succeed you will have delegation, planning, organisational and motivational skills, be committed to on-going education and self-directed learning, and effectively communicate and educate patients, family and staff.

Availability across all shifts including AM - PM - ND both during the week and weekends is required for this position.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer you

Salary: $120,835 to $124,903 (pro rata for part time), plus 12% superannuation

Part Time position, open to job share if multiple suitable candidates are found

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A welcoming and supportive culture

Dynamic multidisciplinary team

Discounts on hospital services and health insurance

Additional professional development

Role: Graphic Designer 
Company Name: MONICA PRINT STORE PTY LTD
Address : 23 Fourth Street, Wingfield, SA 5013
Position: Full-time
Salary Range: $80,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation

ABOUT US
Monica Print Store is a leading signage and printing company based in Adelaide, providing a wide range of high-quality printing, signage, display, and graphic design services to businesses across Australia. We are currently seeking a creative and experienced Graphic Designer to join our growing team. This is a full-time, permanent position based in Wingfield, Adelaide.

The successful candidate will be responsible for producing high-quality visual designs for both print and digital applications.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
•	Consult with clients and stakeholders to clearly determine the objectives, target audience, and constraints of each design brief, ensuring alignment with business goals and brand standards.

•	Conduct thorough research and analysis of functional communication requirements, including market trends, competitor benchmarks, and user needs, to inform creative direction.

•	Develop and formulate innovative design concepts that effectively communicate the intended message across various media and platforms.

•	Prepare detailed mock-ups, illustrations, and layouts to visually present design concepts and proposed solutions for client and team review.

•	Collaborate and negotiate design solutions with clients, management, sales teams, and production staff to ensure feasibility, functionality, and alignment with project objectives.

•	Select and recommend suitable materials, media, typography, and visual styles that meet both aesthetic and functional requirements for publication, digital delivery, or physical display.

•	Document and finalise all technical specifications and design details required for production, ensuring accuracy and compliance with project requirements.

•	Oversee or actively participate in the production process, ensuring design integrity and quality are maintained across chosen media, whether print, digital, or interactive platforms.

•	Maintain and archive project files, design assets, and relevant documentation to support brand consistency and enable future client or internal use.

TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL REQUIRE:
•	Bachelor Degree or higher education in related discipline is required
•	Applicant must have a minimum of 3 years of full-time or equivalent relevant work experience. 
•	Strong skills in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign)
•	Experience working in a fast-paced printing or signage environment is desirable
•	Excellent attention to detail and strong layout/design principles
•	Good communication skills and the ability to work independently and in a team
•	Full time working rights in Australia
•	Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident are encouraged to apply.

BENEFITS OF WORKING WITH US:
•	Competitive Salary Package – Attractive remuneration based on skills and experience. Reward your hard work with annual performance perks (subject to eligibility)
•	Career Growth & Development – Ongoing training, upskilling, and career progression opportunities.
•	Supportive Work Environment – Work with a professional and friendly team that values collaboration and respect.
•	Job Security – A stable and long-term employment opportunity in a growing industry

Maintenance Planner position available in all states NSW, Qld, Vic, & WA

At NEPEAN™ we are proud to be Australia’s leading privately owned engineering, mining services and industrial manufacturing organisation. We have unique capabilities to deliver high value, innovative and sustainable solutions for the world’s leading mining, construction, and transport companies. Over the last 40 years, hard work, technical credibility, and a willingness to tackle very difficult projects have earned NEPEAN an enviable reputation. Today our organisation employs over 1400 people across six continents and distributes products to more than 65 countries.

We service our customers in all states of Australia through multiple businesses in our portfolio: NEPEAN Building and Infrastructure (Galserv, Galintel, Weldlok), NEPEAN Engineering and Innovation, NEPEAN Power, Mining (NEPEAN Longwall), PROK, NEPEAN Conveyors, NEPEAN Transport, Gurtec, Roxon, and NEPEAN Belting Mackay with business locations in Queensland, New South Wales and Western Australia.

Our Opportunity
We are looking for an experienced Maintenance Planner to join our team, bringing a goal-oriented mindset to ensure minimal disruption to the organisation's assets and projects. This role aims to achieve planned time, cost, and quality metrics for projects, aligning with NEPEAN Conveyor’s policies and procedures. The Maintenance Planner will be responsible for strategising, scheduling, coordinating, and monitoring the maintenance of all plant equipment, infrastructure, and machinery - minimizing downtime, reducing costs, and improving overall operational efficiency

Core responsibilities include however are not limited to:
Planning and Scheduling: Develop and manage detailed maintenance schedules and work orders to ensure timely and cost-efficient maintenance of the organisation’s activities and goals.
Coordination: Work closely with maintenance personnel, engineering teams, and operations to schedule regular preventive maintenance, handle emergencies, and conduct inspections. Ensuring minimal disruption to production or services.
Safety Compliance: Ensure that all maintenance work complies with safety regulations and industry standards.
Record Keeping: Maintain accurate records of maintenance performed, equipment condition, and maintenance costs.
Equipment Modifications: Plan and implement equipment modifications and upgrades in collaboration with engineering and operations teams.
Inventory Management: Track the inventory of spare parts and ensure their availability for routine and emergency maintenance.
Problem-Solving: Identify and address potential issues before they become costly problems, and adjust schedules to account for unexpected emergency work.
Reporting: Prepare and present reports on maintenance activities and their effectiveness.

The Right Person
We are interested in hearing from you if you have:
A degree or certificate in a related field such as engineering, industrial maintenance, or facilities management.
Prior experience in facilities maintenance, industrial maintenance, or a similar field.
Strong understanding of maintenance procedures, best practices, and equipment.
Excellent organisational and planning skills to manage schedules and coordinate maintenance activities.
Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively collaborate with maintenance personnel, and engineering teams.
Ability to identify and address potential issues proactively.
Familiarity with maintenance management software and other relevant tools.
Knowledge of safety regulations and protocols to ensure compliance during maintenance activities.
Meticulous attention to detail for accurate record-keeping and reporting.

NEPEAN believes in diversity and is committed to providing Equal Employment opportunities for all applicants. We welcome applicants from all walks of life, including various socio-economic, cultural, LGBTIQ, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander backgrounds

If you're ready for your next challenge, please "Apply Now" and forward through your interest today!
Salary: $130,000 per annum

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen.

We're a well-respected not-for-profit that's been serving society's most vulnerable for over 170 years. Each year, we achieve life-changing outcomes for more than 40,000 people who rely on our person-centred support. And now, we're extending our reach and impact even further.

As a Senior Case Manager - Supporting Recovery, you'll be key to our mission to enrich lives and strengthen communities. Working within our Community & Mission team, you'll provide trauma-informed, recovery-oriented case management to victim-survivors of family, domestic and sexual violence (FDSV), supporting people to move beyond crisis and achieve their recovery goals.

Be welcomed into a compassionate, respectful and purpose-driven community where we don't just talk about values-we live them.

Your opportunity

As our Senior Case Manager - Supporting Recovery, you will provide specialist case management to victim-survivors of family, domestic and sexual violence who are in the recovery phase following crisis. Through comprehensive assessment, collaborative recovery planning, advocacy and service coordination, you'll empower clients to achieve meaningful recovery outcomes while ensuring services are delivered safely, ethically and in line with best practice.

You'll also provide leadership across the Supporting Recovery Program by mentoring case managers, contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and supporting complex decision-making that strengthens outcomes for both clients and the broader service.

With integrity and resilience, you will:

Deliver trauma-informed, recovery-oriented case management to clients with complex needs.

Lead the management of high-risk and complex cases while mentoring fellow practitioners.

Develop collaborative recovery plans through assessment, advocacy and coordinated service delivery.

Build strong partnerships with clients, CatholicCare, NSW Health and specialist agencies.

Contribute to continuous improvement and best-practice service delivery.

What you'll bring

You are an experienced, compassionate and resilient case management professional who thrives in complex environments and shares our values of Integrity, Justice, Compassion and Excellence.

You will also need:

University qualification in Social Work, Psychology, Welfare or Community Services.

Minimum three years' experience in family and domestic violence recovery case management.

Experience managing complex cases involving trauma, mental health and intersecting vulnerabilities.

Current NSW Driver Licence.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Ideally, you will also have:

AASW social work accreditation

Leadership and mentoring experience.

Knowledge of OOHC legislation and child protection practices.

Experience in trauma-informed and recovery-oriented practice.

Strong stakeholder engagement skills.

Confidence managing high-risk situations.

Why Anglicare?

We provide meaningful opportunities and choice, both for the individuals and communities we support and the dedicated people here who make it happen.

At Anglicare, you'll get the security, stability and opportunities that come with a strong, well-established organisation that's ready for the future. You'll belong to a community of kind, humble and respectful people of all faiths and backgrounds. You will also be supported to gain new knowledge, deepen your experience and expertise, and shape a rewarding career.

Pay less tax with salary packaging.

Up to $2,650 tax free for meals and entertainment.

Ongoing professional development and leadership training.

Exclusive discounts with over 400 retailers.

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport.

We're many services, with one purpose, to meet people where they are and walk with them. At Anglicare, we believe everyone is Made for Connection, with God, with each other, and with the places we call home. But sometimes, life unravels. That's where we step in, in Community and Mission, offering hope, support, and presence. From food relief to chaplaincy, crisis care to caring for the wellbeing of the elderly, every moment of connection matters. And it's not just what we do. It's how we do it: side-by-side, with compassion and care.

Are you ready for a career that means more?

To apply for this role, please click the Apply button and submit your r sum and cover letter. All applicants will receive a response.

Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the customers and communities we support. While we are guided by our Christian-based values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds who share our commitment to serving others. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders, abilities and cultural backgrounds.

Southern Steel Group and its subsidiaries specialise in providing the nest steel products, sheet & coil, and expert steel processing and distribution. Our company network is extensive, represented in every Australian state.

Southern Queensland Steel is part of the Southern Steel Group, the largest privately-owned steel company in Australia. With more than 1400 employees nationwide, the foundations of this company are built on strong values and a sense of family belonging.

We service our customers through multiple SQS businesses and division affiliates in various States in Australia. In NSW: Steelpipes, Piling Solutions Australia, Rigby Jones, Rollco, Metal Shop Technics, Southern Sheet & Coil, Coil Processors. In QLD: RPG Australia. In Victoria: Surdex Steel, Smithweld Bending, KOMO Metform Engineering, Alliance Laser, Surdex Sheet & Coil, Eliott Engineering, Australian Rollforming Manufacturers. In SA: Brice Metals, Ferrocut. In WA: WA Cutting Services, Boyd Metal Industries

To succeed in this position, you will need to have industry related experience within similar positions, a strong work ethic and strong safety focus.

The ability to carry out work with minimal supervision, a keen and enthusiastic approach to your work and willingness to work over time will help you ensure success in this role.

MAIN OBJECTIVE
Responsible for managing engineering and production processes of jobs from quoting stage to completion, including planning, scheduling, NC programming, purchasing, follow up, liaising with customers, suppliers and coordinating with other team members during entire production process.

DUTIES
Review quotation and purchase order information (provide assistance to Estimator during quotation process if required). Enter sales order and set up jobs in ERP system. Update job information in relevant customer folder.
Process CAD information using AUTOCAD to put through FAST CAM package to generate NC Programs to relevant machines. Convert 3D drawings to 2D if relevant.
Calculate material required and check availability of stock (obtain quote & source material if necessary).
Keep system job entries up-to-date. Transfer relevant NC programs to machines. Issue Job Card to Workshop.
Constantly follow progress of jobs, check engineering, tooling and quality. Ensure completed job complies with customer requirements. Liaise with customers regarding job completion and delivery status.
Coordinate with Accounts and Production Manager to ensure jobs are shipped and invoiced upon completion.
Conduct job analysis on time, cost, quality and materials. Make any changes/improvements as required for future jobs.
Liaise with other team members regarding current jobs, quoted/potential jobs, production issues relating to machines, operators, material etc.
Other indirect tasks as directed by Manager including: coordinating IT services with HO; changing crystal report in Ml to suit our application; suggest Improvements/streamline processes; provide customer information to team members to assist with obtaining future work.
All employees are subject to legal obligations regarding their own and their fellow workers Work Health & Safety (WH&S). They are to fully co-operate with the company WH&S Policy and Program, to ensure safety in the workplace is maintained. All employees shall undertake hazard identification as part of their normal duties, and report any unsafe conditions or work practices. All employees are responsible for their own safety as well as those around them.

SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED
Sound knowledge, understanding and interpretation of engineering drawings
Knowledge and experience in cutting and forming processes
Meticulous — eye for detail
Understand and utilise computer technology (AUTOCAD / FASTCAM)
Excellent communication skills
Strong work ethic and values team work

The successful applicant will be joining a secure, reputable organisation who o er their employees’ opportunities for career progression.

A.B.N. 20 143 358 963
Job Location: 10 Rosedale Avenue, Greenacre, NSW, 2190,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 20 Jul 2026 > 17 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1691-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client MNI ElectroSpark All Trades Services Pty Limited is seeking to add an Accountant to its Greenacre-based operations. The position will support accurate financial reporting, statutory compliance, budgeting, payroll, project costing and management decision-making across a busy multi-trade services environment. The successful appointee will help strengthen financial controls, improve reporting processes and maintain reliable accounting systems as the business continues to grow.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements and management reports.
- Manage accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll processing and general ledger reconciliations.
- Prepare budgets, forecasts and financial models supporting operational and strategic business objectives.
- Monitor project costs, revenue, margins and financial performance across multiple trade contracts.
- Complete month-end processes, including journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Prepare and review BAS, GST, PAYG, payroll and other statutory reporting obligations.
- Maintain accurate job costing records for labour, materials, subcontractors and individual work orders.
- Investigate financial variances and provide practical recommendations to improve profitability and efficiency.
- Develop and maintain effective internal controls protecting company assets and financial information.
- Coordinate audit requirements and respond to queries from auditors, advisers and regulatory authorities.
- Liaise with project managers regarding billing, timesheets, purchase orders and cost discrepancies.
- Maintain and improve accounting systems, reporting tools and automated financial processes.
- Monitor cash flow, outstanding invoices, supplier payments and short-term funding requirements.
- Provide timely financial insights and reports supporting management planning and decision-making.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- Relevant bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in accounting, finance or a closely related professional discipline.
- At least three years’ demonstrated accounting experience, preferably within trades, contracting, project-based or multi-service business environments.
- Strong experience in preparing financial statements, management reports, budgets, forecasts, reconciliations and statutory reporting obligations.
- Practical knowledge of Australian taxation and compliance requirements, including BAS, GST, PAYG, payroll and superannuation.
- Demonstrated ability to manage accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, month-end processes and general ledger integrity.
- Proficiency with accounting software such as Xero or MYOB, together with advanced Microsoft Excel capabilities.
- Strong analytical skills for reviewing project costs, financial performance, variances, cash flow and operational efficiency.
- Excellent communication, organisational and stakeholder management skills, with accuracy and discretion when handling confidential financial information.

Please include Reference: J1691-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

We are seeking a motivated team member to join us in a part-time role 19 hours per week, Monday to Friday. We can offer flexibility in how these hours are worked, with the opportunity to negotiate a roster that suits both you and the needs of the service.

Proven ability to provide effective leadership-decision-making in clinical issues management; and leadership qualities and ability to motivate staff and generate networks

Demonstrated knowledge, understanding and commitment to quality and risk management.
